# Nexus

> Connect your agents once. Link your services once.

Nexus is the single place where AI coding agents connect and the single place where
services are linked. It works out which project an agent is working in and routes every
call to the correct account and resource, so an agent can never reach another project's
services. Built for a solo developer running several agents (Claude Code, Codex,
OpenCode, and others) across several of their own projects. Status: MVP in progress,
Linux first. Source of truth: the Notion paper "Nexus — Product & Technical Strategy".

## How it works

Agent → Session → Project → Environment → Service → Account → Resource → Capability

1. Ask: the agent asks Nexus for a capability. It does not choose the project or credentials.
2. Resolve (core routing, always on): Nexus resolves project and environment, then the bound
   account and resource. No match, no registration, or an ambiguous signal is refused before
   anything reaches a provider.
3. Forward: Nexus relays the call with the bound account's credentials. Agents never hold keys.
4. Log: routing decisions and forwarded calls go to a local, secret-free activity log.

- Supabase + Project A ≠ Supabase + Project B
- Supabase + Production ≠ Supabase + Development
- Supabase Account 1 + Resource X ≠ Supabase Account 2 + Resource X

## MVP scope

- Local desktop app and runtime (Linux first)
- Project registry with `.nexus/project.json` (authoritative, secret-free)
- Starting catalog of about 50 services (proposal, under review). Native adapters: Supabase, GitHub.
  Others are Curated (generic MCP forwarding) or Self-added.
- Services tab (link accounts once), Agents tab (connect and import agent CLIs), Bindings per project
- All agents connect to one persistent local Nexus over HTTP (`http://localhost:<port>/mcp`)
- Concurrent, isolated agent sessions; local activity log; topology view with drag-to-link and confirm
- Agent-facing MCP surface: `nexus.context`, `nexus.request_access`, `nexus.execute`
- Dark and light themes

## Not in the MVP

- Guard (allow / warn / require approval / block, spend limits): post-MVP, possible paid feature
- Catalog beyond ~50 services, SSO, RBAC, team features, compliance dashboards

## What Nexus is not

- Not a vault or password manager
- Not an enterprise governance or compliance platform
- Not a filesystem sandbox; its boundary is infrastructure access
- An action outside Nexus is unmanaged, not protected

## Honest limits

- Native adapters (Supabase, GitHub) can pin calls to the bound resource.
- Curated and Self-added services currently get account-level isolation, not resource-level.
  Use one account per project for those.

## Pricing (proposal, not final)

Free: up to 2 projects with core routing. Pro: about $10–12/month or $99/year. Team/Agency: later.
Core routing stays free by design.
